title: Pointwise CATE Estimation under Locally Vanishing Overlap and Rough Nuisances
banked_reason: The delivered contribution remains too specialized and incomplete for field tier; the exact-uniform nuisance-dominated converse needed for a new bounded-overlap minimax characterization is absent.
gap_reasons: The note proves a sharp supplied-propensity rate for every κ and an unknown-propensity oracle-rate result only in the relatively smooth region α+β≥γ; elsewhere for κ>0 it delivers only a first-order bracket, leaving the principal higher-order frontier, logarithmic boundaries, and oracle-penalty classification open.

Its κ=0 higher-order rate and elbow are expressly already covered by Kennedy–Balakrishnan–Robins–Wasserman, so totalization and exact-uniform implementation are incremental rather than a new rate result.
The delivered contribution remains too specialized and incomplete for the field tier or a projected leading-journal score of 7.8.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the all-κ supplied-propensity minimax rate, a total first-order unknown-propensity bracket, and a total exact-uniform second-order estimator at κ=0 that attains the oracle rate at and above the nuisance elbow. The attempted field-tier completion failed at the matching fixed-n Bernoulli product-mixture converse below that elbow: disjoint bumps violate γ-Hölder smoothness, overlapping frames lose partition locality, and filling support holes leaves a divergent n h^d δ² term. A future retry must prove that converse or derive and match a corrected rate, then complete the κ>0 higher-order frontier.
tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the sharp supplied-propensity theorem gives \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) for every \(\kappa\geq0\) by an explicit annular estimator and genuine full-support exact-uniform Bernoulli lower laws.  The total data-only first-order estimator gives \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\leq R_n\leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At bounded overlap, KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE already covers the same higher-order upper rate and nuisance elbow and applies to known uniform design.  This note therefore presents its \(\kappa=0\) result only as an explicitly total one-sided exact-uniform specialization using the known Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback.  That specialization gives \(R_n\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\), with \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))\), and matches the supplied-propensity lower bound when \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including equality without a logarithm.  Below that elbow only the exact-uniform nuisance converse remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order frontier and critical logarithms remain open.
gap: The closest pointwise CATE minimax theorem assumes bounded overlap and uses a support-modified fuzzy lower construction; weak-overlap work instead treats average effects or scalar regression, and recent propensity-free pointwise RKHS theory retains a global overlap lower bound.
fill: The project derives a same-class matched minimax rate, an oracle-versus-unknown phase diagram, all critical logarithms, a total finite-operation estimator, and a full-support fixed-\(n\) Bernoulli product-mixture converse.
